newsitem.title: USA: Wet weather virtually halts Kansas fieldwork.
newsitem.headline: Wet weather virtually halts Kansas fieldwork.

text.p: Kansas farmers made little progress with fall harvest and wheat seedings as wet weather prevailed during the week ended Sunday, the weekly state crop report said.

The report said wheat acreage remains to be seeded in the east central and southeastern districts. Wheat diseases such as stem and leaf rust, wheat streak mosaic and septoria continued to be found over much of the state.
For the third consecutive week, wheat seeding was listed as only 99 percent complete. That compared to 100 percent a year ago and 99 percent for the five-year average.
Wheat was 98 percent emerged, versus 98 last week, 96 last year and 95 on average.
Kansas wheat was rated 90 percent good to excellent, versus 89 percent at that level last week.
Corn was 99 percent harvested versus 98 last week, 100 last year and the average of 98 percent.
Sorghum was 95 percent harvested, versus 94 last week, 100 last year and the average of 92 percent. Soybeans were 92 percent harvested, versus 94 last week, 100 last year and 98 on average.
Pasture condition was rated 69 percent good to excellent, versus 69 at that level last week.
